<reason>PRO built a clean normative spine (centrality of the church actors, institutional continuity of property, shared perpetration, "otherwise victims are invoiced for their own abuse") and its best counterpunch — that the Canadian and Irish failures indict voluntary/indemnified deals, not enforceable assessed contribution — was a genuine reversal. But CON did the harder comparative work. It pre-empted the enforceability repair (the Canadian collapse ended in court; the Irish indemnity was legally binding, so the missing ingredient was a unitary solvent defendant, not better drafting), and it turned PRO's strongest device against it: "no archives, no discharge" means selling finality certified against an index the defendant itself supplied — i.e. Ireland with a better preface. CON then exploited PRO's own concession that the fund "pays now from state seed money," collapsing the speed and compensation differences and reducing PRO's marginal benefit to a later treasury reimbursement purchased with permanent release. CON's Pressure Question answers were honest and directly labelled ("I never called them penniless — not unitary, not liquid"), and it offered a non-consensual leverage alternative (subpoena, criminalised destruction, conditioning tax exemption and land title) that PRO only dismissed as "hope" without dismantling. PRO scored real hits — "land is money" (CON conceded transfer of property, distinguishing only restitution in rem), and the point that obstruction which is cheap will continue — but PRO dropped the land concession by the closing and never exposed the latent problem that CON's certification objection would equally defeat any subpoena regime. CON's Rebuttal 1 clipping is a real execution cost, but the surviving text carried its weighing. Net: CON made the decision easier to reach.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON's demonstration that PRO's "no archives, no discharge" fund is structurally the Irish indemnity — finality granted against a disclosure the church itself curates and indexes — combined with the exploitation of PRO's admission that the fund pays survivors from state seed money, which stripped PRO of the speed and compensation advantages and left only a treasury reimbursement bought with permanent release.</best_rebuttal>
